sourcePins.role: Host research system; this lane is presently untracked and therefore not commit-pinned evidence.
Current BCH consensus, policy, introspection, and VM-limit authority for experiments.
Independent transaction, VM, operation-cost, and canonical-encoding cross-check. SHA-256 is the tooling manifest, not a clean-tree digest.
Real transaction packaging, historical Circle work, mutation, and verifier benchmark patterns; never pool qualification authority.
BCH Script optimization and transaction-context tooling after semantic kernels are fixed.
Architecture calculus and cheap lower-bound/falsification pattern; projections cannot qualify bytes.
Reuse gate for locally available BCH and ZK tools.
Exact nontrivial factorization which eliminates the intended 2^29-1 base-field control.
Complete neutral-M31 fixed4 codec and base-arithmetic corpus across standard Libauth, the real BCHN standard-script leg, and LeanBCH verdict/cost surfaces; not extension or proof evidence.
Circle-domain FRI construction and arbitrary CFFT-friendly-field prior art.

Exact current IACR PDF bytes after the final 2025-02-22 revision; design-warning source for witness masking, quotient decomposition, FRI-view leakage, and permutation arguments, not a complete PoolActionFv1 ZK construction.
Historical initial RPO-M31/XHash-M31 construction input only; the current official page says this paper was merged into ePrint 2023/1045 and directs readers to the merged version.
Pre-merge historical XHash-family PDF only; it predates the current 2026 merged M31 revision and cannot authorize current parameters.
Official metadata revised 2026-05-15; authority for the merge/supersession notice, not construction contents.
Official current merged-paper metadata revised 2026-05-11; identifies current M31-family claims but is not the full security or parameter source.
Current merged XHash-family construction and security source; exact current PDF bytes must be content-pinned before an RPO-M31/XHash-M31-derived selection.
100-bit, single-seed, non-PoolAction Goldilocks packaging and mutation control near the transaction ceiling.

rows.candidate: M31 base-field codec and arithmetic control
rows.description: Shared p = 2^31 - 1 base-field substrate used to attribute codec and BCH arithmetic evidence without pretending that a degree-4, degree-5, or degree-6 extension has been selected.
assumptions: Strict four-byte unsigned little-endian values are rejected at or above p before they can alias through BCH ScriptNum conversion.
requiredMeasurements: native reference KATs and canonical rejection corpus
real BCH-2026 decode, add, subtract, multiply, square, and inverse-hint kernels
independent raw-metric agreement where LeanBCH supports every used opcode

cheapKillGate.method: Cross-check strict base-field KATs, deterministic random/low-range/boundary relations, and every-position ScriptNum-alias mutations in the native reference, Libauth BCH-2026 VM, BCHN standard-script leg, and LeanBCH where supported.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: All valid boundaries agree, every noncanonical fixed4 alias rejects, and exact kernel bytes and raw metrics are recorded.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate only to concrete extension rows after the shared base codec and arithmetic gate passes; this row is never a complete proof tuple.

rows.candidate: M31 with a canonical degree-4 extension
rows.description: Conventional CM31/QM31-style prior art. One extension element carries under 128 raw bits, so the complete derivation must show whether multiple challenges avoid a systemic cap.
assumptions: An irreducible tower and canonical 4-limb encoding exist.
Field-size losses are counted rather than hidden by grinding.
requiredMeasurements: base and extension add, multiply, square, inverse, decode, and challenge-sampling BCH kernels

cheapKillGate.method: Derive every field-capacity and union-bound term before implementing the AIR.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: A concrete 128-bit systemic bound exists without treating approximately 124 raw field bits as 128.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate only if the soundness worksheet passes and exact Script kernels fit the per-input budget.

rows.candidate: M31 with a degree-5 extension
rows.description: Approximately 155 raw extension-field bits offer target headroom, at the cost of a nonstandard tower and five-limb verifier arithmetic.
assumptions: A low-cost irreducible construction and efficient inversion strategy can be found.
Odd-degree tower handling does not dominate the verifier.

cheapKillGate.method: Implement canonical arithmetic KATs and one extension multiplication/inversion verification kernel.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: All edge cases agree across native reference and BCH VM, and one-query lower bounds remain plausible.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate to Circle and transcript kernels after algebra and capacity gates pass.

rows.candidate: M31 with a degree-6 extension
rows.description: Approximately 186 raw field bits provide more union-bound margin but add limbs and proof bytes.
assumptions: A quadratic-over-cubic or cubic-over-quadratic tower is efficient and canonical.
requiredMeasurements: six-limb Script bytes and operation cost
proof-byte impact per opening and challenge

cheapKillGate.method: Compare one exact extension fold and inverse-check kernel with degree 5.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: Added capacity is not dominated by transaction bytes or operation cost before full AIR work.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate only if it is non-dominated on capacity, bytes, and verifier cost.

rows.candidate: M61 with a quadratic extension
rows.description: Two 61-bit limbs remain below 128 raw bits and may incur awkward signed-64-bit multiplication handling in BCH Script.
assumptions: Canonical limb arithmetic can avoid every signed overflow and alternate representation.

cheapKillGate.method: Run boundary KATs and derive the target capacity before Circle FFT work.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: No VM overflow ambiguity and a concrete path to 128 systemic bits.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate only if it is not capacity-capped or Script-dominated.

rows.candidate: M61 with a cubic extension
rows.description: Approximately 183 raw bits with three wider limbs; potential fewer limbs than high-degree M31 but harder base multiplication.
assumptions: Cubic extension arithmetic and M61 reduction can be verified cheaply enough on BCH.
requiredMeasurements: M61 base and cubic extension kernels

cheapKillGate.method: Measure one complete extension fold and inverse-check under real BCH VM rules.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: Measured compound cost remains competitive with M31 degree-5/6 candidates.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate after native prover and real Script kernels both pass.

rows.candidate: p = 2^29 - 1 with a degree-5 extension (invalid field control)
rows.description: The intended Mersenne modulus is 536870911 = 233 * 1103 * 2089, so it is composite and cannot define the proposed base field.
requiredMeasurements: No implementation measurement: the exact compositeness certificate kills this candidate before benchmarking.

cheapKillGate.method: Verify that the intended base modulus is prime before any field or Circle-domain implementation.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: The intended p = 2^29 - 1 modulus is prime.

rows.escalationCondition: Do not escalate this row; introduce any different approximately 29-bit prime as a new precisely named candidate.

elimination.reason: The proposed modulus is composite, so arithmetic modulo it is not a field and the Circle-FRI field assumptions do not apply.
elimination.reopeningCondition: Never for p = 2^29 - 1; a different prime requires a new candidate row and fresh domain and soundness analysis.

rows.candidate: M127 with a quadratic extension
rows.description: Wide-base control with ample capacity but multi-limb base arithmetic likely hostile to BCH Script.
assumptions: The base field is CFFT-friendly for the required domain and a correct multi-limb implementation is feasible.
requiredMeasurements: circle operation and proof-width lower bound

cheapKillGate.method: Compile one canonical multiply/reduce and Circle-point check before any prover work.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: The one-query lower bound is not already dominated by narrower-field candidates.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate only if the presumed Script penalty is falsified.

rows.candidate: J-symmetric twin circle domain
rows.description: Primary Circle-STARK domain family with explicit twin handling and x-fiber soundness tests.
assumptions: Generator order, vanishing polynomial, and trace/evaluation separation are derived for each base field.
requiredMeasurements: J-twin and x-fiber selector adversarial tests

cheapKillGate.method: Enumerate a small complete domain and validate generator, twins, vanishing zeros, and selector support.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: No duplicate, unintended zero fiber, off-domain acceptance, or transition-selector alias exists.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate to full-size domains only after exhaustive small-domain checks pass.

rows.candidate: Rotation-subgroup Circle domain
rows.description: Alternative trace-step mapping to compare next-row and verifier arithmetic against J-symmetric encoding.
assumptions: A canonical point representation and exact subgroup check are available.

cheapKillGate.method: Compare exhaustive small-domain semantics and one BCH rotation kernel with the J-symmetric candidate.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: No semantic mismatch and a non-dominated exact cost exists.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate only if it reduces total AIR or verifier cost without a selector hazard.

rows.candidate: BCH-native SHA-256 with role-specific domain separation
rows.description: Native verifier-friendly candidate for proof Merkle trees, transcript, context, note, and nullifier roles; prover/AIR costs must be separated by role.
assumptions: SHA-256 collision, preimage, and random-oracle-style transcript assumptions are stated per role.
Domain tags and length encodings are unambiguous.
requiredMeasurements: prover throughput and AIR impact where used inside the relation

cheapKillGate.method: Measure native hash iterations and exact proof-path bytes for each proposed role.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: All role encodings are canonical and complete-query density fits current standard budgets.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate role by role; do not require one hash to serve every role.

rows.candidate: BCH-native double SHA-256
rows.description: Native compatibility control; extra hashing may be dominated unless it removes another binding or implementation risk.
assumptions: Double hashing provides a measurable system benefit for the selected role.

cheapKillGate.method: Compare identical domain-separated messages in the real compound-query kernel.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: A concrete security or byte advantage justifies the additional digest round.

rows.escalationCondition: Remain a control unless a role-specific advantage is measured.

rows.candidate: Widened RPO-M31 or XHash-M31-style algebraic hash
rows.description: AIR/prover-oriented candidate. Stock parameter widths must not be relabeled 128-bit; a widened construction and BCH verifier implementation need fresh analysis.
assumptions: A widened construction has a defensible 128-bit binding analysis.
Custom BCH arithmetic is not transaction-dominating.

cheapKillGate.method: Pin the current merged source, derive width/capacity security, and compile one permutation under BCH rules.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: At least 128-bit role security and a non-dominated complete-query lower bound.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate only after source pinning and both security and Script gates pass.

rows.candidate: Poseidon2-style M31 arithmetic hash
rows.description: AIR-friendly comparison whose custom BCH Script cost and exact security parameters are unknown.
assumptions: A parameter generator, constants, security analysis, and canonical digest packing are pinned.
requiredMeasurements: full-round permutation bytes and operation cost

cheapKillGate.method: Compile and execute one full selected permutation, not an operation-count projection.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: Measured total cost beats native SHA-256 after AIR and proof effects are included.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate only with exact parameters and a total-system advantage.

rows.candidate: HASH160 for binding commitments
rows.description: A 160-bit digest provides only about 80-bit generic collision resistance and cannot carry a 128-bit binding role.

cheapKillGate.method: Compare digest width with the 128-bit collision target.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: At least 256 digest bits for an ideal 128-bit collision target.

rows.escalationCondition: May reopen only for a non-binding auxiliary role with a separately justified security requirement.

elimination.reason: Digest width is below the binding target.
elimination.reopeningCondition: The role is proven non-binding and isolated from systemic soundness.

rows.candidate: Fresh randomized trace and composition masking preserved through the full FRI view
rows.description: Primary ZK research family; masking is co-designed with degree bounds, commitments, folding, queries, and repeated proofs.
assumptions: Fresh entropy is independent per proof.
A simulator or indistinguishability bound covers every opened and folded object.

cheapKillGate.method: Complete the ZK leakage schema for every committed/opened object before performance work.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: Constraint preservation, folding preservation, fresh entropy, simulator claim, and mask-reuse failure tests are all supported.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate only after the complete leakage worksheet and root/SOL review.

rows.candidate: Random low-degree quotient masks multiplied by the constraint vanishing polynomial
rows.description: Candidate component, not a complete ZK claim; must show what remains hidden after composition and FRI openings.
assumptions: Masks preserve all constraints and sufficient entropy survives every opening.
requiredMeasurements: added degree, rows, commitments, openings, proof bytes, time, and RSS

cheapKillGate.method: Symbolically and empirically test constraint and fold behavior on a small complete protocol instance.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: No witness-dependent statistic remains outside the declared public statement.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate only as part of a complete masking construction.

rows.candidate: Per-leaf random salts without algebraic trace masking
rows.description: Control to test whether Merkle hiding alone fails to hide algebraic openings and folded codewords.
assumptions: Salts are freshly generated and committed.

cheapKillGate.method: Run the leakage worksheet against all non-Merkle algebraic observations.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: Every witness-dependent observation is simulated, not only unopened leaves.

rows.escalationCondition: Expected to remain auxiliary unless the full leakage argument passes.

rows.candidate: No witness masking
rows.description: Unmasked witness commitments are incompatible with a shielded withdrawal.
requiredMeasurements: none; this is a negative control

cheapKillGate.method: Compare candidate behavior with the mandatory zero-knowledge goal.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: Explicit witness hiding is present.

rows.escalationCondition: Never reopen for withdrawal.

elimination.reason: Fails the mandatory zero-knowledge relation goal.

rows.candidate: One AIR with a canonical deposit/withdrawal selector
rows.description: Shares codecs and verifier logic but risks selector cross-action confusion and unused-column overhead.
assumptions: The selector is boolean and every action-inactive field is canonically constrained.
requiredMeasurements: trace width, rows, degree, quotient count, proof openings, and action-confusion mutations

cheapKillGate.method: Build a semantic oracle and mutate selector plus every inactive field before Circle-FRI implementation.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: No mixed-action witness satisfies the relation and total cost is competitive.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate after semantic-vector and degree-bound review.

rows.candidate: Separate deposit and withdrawal AIR programs under one proof protocol
rows.description: Avoids selector ambiguity and may reduce per-action trace width while duplicating verifier metadata or code.
assumptions: Program identity is immutably bound by the security profile and action statement.

cheapKillGate.method: Compare exact symbolic constraint counts and program-binding bytes with unified AIR.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: No cross-program replay and at least one measured total-cost advantage.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate the non-dominated program layout after primitive costs are known.

rows.candidate: Separate transition, boundary, state-binding, accumulator, and conservation quotients
rows.description: Makes responsibility coverage explicit but may add roots and openings relative to a unified composition.
assumptions: Every quotient is independently transcript-bound and included in the soundness union bound.

cheapKillGate.method: Produce a responsibility-to-constraint map and symbolic opening count.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: No responsibility is omitted and added openings are not dominated by unified composition.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate only after exact hash and field costs exist.

rows.candidate: Binary Circle-FRI folding
rows.description: More rounds with simple folds and authentication structure.
assumptions: The exact Circle partner map and challenge schedule are canonical.
requiredMeasurements: round, root, path, and final-polynomial bytes

cheapKillGate.method: Package one transcript-derived query including Merkle path, fold, and final check in real P2SH32.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: Real VM acceptance and a lower bound compatible with one complete 128-bit transaction.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate after one-query and soundness gates pass.

rows.candidate: Arity-4 Circle-FRI folding
rows.description: Fewer rounds with wider per-fold arithmetic and multiproof tradeoffs.
assumptions: Arity-4 folding has a complete soundness reduction for the selected domain and query schedule.

cheapKillGate.method: Compare one exact query and derived security tuple against binary folding.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: Non-dominated complete-query bytes/op-cost with no soundness shortcut.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate only from measured compound-query evidence.

rows.candidate: Arity-8 Circle-FRI folding
rows.description: Aggressive round reduction with wider folds and potentially larger query openings.
assumptions: Arity-8 domain, folding, and query soundness are derived rather than borrowed from Goldilocks controls.

cheapKillGate.method: Measure a complete arity-8 query before any full prover implementation.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: It beats binary/arity-4 total cost at equal derived security and canonical parsing.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate only if equal-security measured evidence is non-dominated.

rows.candidate: Sparse Merkle set keyed by the full nullifier
rows.description: Direct non-membership through an empty leaf, with fixed-depth paths and potentially high AIR hash cost.
assumptions: Key-bit ordering, empty roots, and path depth are canonical and capacity-safe.
requiredMeasurements: non-membership plus insertion AIR rows and proof bytes

cheapKillGate.method: Implement a small semantic set oracle with valid insert and single-bit/path mutations.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: Absent-to-present update is unique, duplicate insertion rejects, and projected path cost is plausible.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate after semantic correctness and hash-cost bounds pass.

rows.candidate: Indexed or sorted Merkle set with predecessor/successor non-membership
rows.description: Shorter paths may trade for comparison, neighbor-update, and canonical-order constraints.
assumptions: Ordering, sentinels, neighbor links, and insertion position are uniquely constrained.

cheapKillGate.method: Exhaustively enumerate small sets and every insertion position against a reference model.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: Exactly one valid successor exists and all duplicate/order attacks reject.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate to AIR only after exhaustive small-set equivalence.

rows.candidate: Append-only nullifier membership tree without authenticated non-membership
rows.description: Appending a public nullifier does not itself prove it was absent and cannot enforce unique spend.

cheapKillGate.method: Attempt a second insertion of an existing nullifier.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: The old-root witness proves absence before insertion.

rows.escalationCondition: Reopen only by adding an authenticated non-membership relation, making it a different candidate.

elimination.reopeningCondition: A complete non-membership and insertion construction is specified.

rows.candidate: Domain-separated owner-secret preimage commitment proven inside the AIR
rows.description: Minimal PQ-oriented private ownership relation; selected hash and encoding must meet preimage/binding targets and wallet-recovery needs.
assumptions: Owner secrets have sufficient entropy and are never reused across incompatible domains.
requiredMeasurements: AIR hash cost and proof impact
wallet derivation, backup, and cross-pool domain tests

cheapKillGate.method: Build canonical derivation KATs and mutate secret, pool, note index, and rho.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: Only the exact owner secret authorizes and all domains produce distinct commitments/nullifiers.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate with the selected role-specific hash and wallet design.

rows.candidate: One-time hash-signature verification inside the AIR
rows.description: More conventional authorization semantics but likely dominated by signature witness and hash volume when proof-of-preimage suffices.
assumptions: A one-time key lifecycle is recoverable and cannot authorize multiple notes incorrectly.
requiredMeasurements: signature witness size, AIR rows, proving time, and recovery state

cheapKillGate.method: Derive the smallest complete signature verification trace and compare it with direct preimage ownership.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: A concrete security or recovery advantage justifies all added cost and state.

rows.escalationCondition: Remain a control unless it solves a demonstrated preimage-authorization defect.

rows.candidate: State plus one persistent verifier carrier input
rows.description: Minimizes carrier bookkeeping but requires the complete verifier role to fit one 10,000-byte locking/unlocking envelope and its cost density.
assumptions: All proof parsing and verification can fit the current per-script and per-input budgets.
requiredMeasurements: one complete query and projected complete verifier per-input bounds

cheapKillGate.method: Compile one complete query plus binding and derive a hard lower bound for all queries and roots.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: Script, element, stack, hash, and operation-cost limits remain feasible without omitted responsibilities.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate only if the hard per-input envelope remains plausible.

rows.candidate: Fixed manifest of persistent verifier carrier inputs recreated by every action
rows.description: Uses multiple current-standard input budgets while preserving one user action and one transaction; adds source/successor bytes and cross-role binding.
assumptions: Every role is required exactly once and verifies one shared proof session.
Carrier values and locks are preserved with no replenisher.
requiredMeasurements: exact empty-shell bytes by carrier count

cheapKillGate.method: Serialize state, every carrier source/successor, payout, funding input, and optional change before proof bytes.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: The shell plus a conservative 128-bit proof lower bound fits 100,000 bytes and every carrier is perpetual.

rows.escalationCondition: Escalate candidate carrier counts only after exact shell and one-query measurements.

rows.candidate: Pre-created finite carrier stock consumed without exact successors
rows.description: Eventually requires replenishment, a coordinator, or an extra setup transaction and violates unilateral persistent operation.

cheapKillGate.method: Follow carrier availability for more actions than the pre-created stock.
cheapKillGate.passCriteria: Every action recreates all required roles without another party or transaction.

rows.escalationCondition: Reopen only as a persistent-successor topology, which is a different row.

elimination.reason: Finite carrier stock violates the no-coordinator and one-transaction lifecycle.
elimination.reopeningCondition: All roles become exact persistent successors.

querySchedules: canonical deduplicated indices with multiplicity accounted
parameterSearchSpace.concreteTupleRule: Every concrete tuple gets its own soundness worksheet, canonical encoding, one-query BCH measurement, proof/transaction byte model, and candidate digest. No Cartesian-product row is selected by a headline formula.

requiredBeforeSelection: PoolActionFv1 semantic oracle and responsibility mutation index
content-pinned primary sources for any selected construction
canonical algebra and parser known-answer tests
measured primitive and compound-query BCH kernels
exact empty-shell and projected complete-transaction bounds
decisionPolicy.fallbackRule: No 100-to-127-bit candidate may be selected until an optimized complete 128-bit deposit and withdrawal are both measured and fail the 100,000-byte standard envelope; root/SOL must then explicitly authorize fallback research.
decisionPolicy.componentEvidenceRule: A component projection may kill an impossible candidate but cannot qualify a field, proof, prover, verifier, or complete transaction.
